title: Kasuwa
tagline: A direct marketplace for agricultural trade
description: A marketplace concept designed to connect agricultural sellers and buyers through a structured digital commerce experience.
summary: Agricultural producers often sell through fragmented channels at opaque prices, while buyers absorb the cost of inconsistent quality and slow negotiation. Kasuwa is a prototype that gives both sides the same structure: listings with real quantities and grades, transparent pricing, and a transaction flow designed for a phone on a farm rather than a desk in an office.
challenge: Fragmented distribution and opaque pricing on the producer side, inconsistent quality and slow negotiation on the buyer side.
approach: Structured listings, transparent vendor communication and a mobile-first transaction flow built around the way trade actually happens.
result: A working interface prototype that turns an informal sale into a legible, repeatable transaction.

title: Liora
tagline: Legal research and document review in one surface
description: A legal technology platform exploring legal research, document review, intelligence and decision support through a unified product experience.
summary: Liora started from a simple observation: legal work is not short of information, it is short of a way to hold it together. Research, statutes, filings and internal documents live in separate tools, so the work becomes a sequence of context switches. The platform puts research, review and decision support in one workspace organised around the matter rather than the tool. I designed the information architecture and interaction model, and built the front end for the research and review surfaces.
challenge: Legal teams cross-referencing multiple jurisdictions spend more time re-establishing context than reading.
approach: A single workspace organised around the matter, with research, review and decision support sharing one navigation model and one citation format.
result: A high-density interface that keeps citations, documents and reasoning in view at the same time.

title: Sotion
tagline: Evidence instead of verdicts for disputed media
description: An early-stage digital media forensics project focused on image verification, reproducible evidence and layered media analysis.
summary: Most authenticity tools promise a true or false answer, which is more than the underlying evidence can support. Sotion reports three things instead: what a file establishes, what the public record says about it, and what no available check can establish. Every finding is an evidence unit carrying the rule that produced it, resolved into a verdict with an explicit statement of its limits. When the general synthetic-detection track failed its pre-registered validation gates, it was closed and documented rather than shipped as an overclaim.
challenge: Detector tools present a true or false verdict that the underlying evidence cannot support.
approach: A pipeline where every finding carries the rule that produced it, from EXIF geometry to compression evidence, copy-move regions and C2PA signature validity.
result: A precision-first product with published evaluation gates and an honest account of what each check does not prove.

title: TradingPal
tagline: Positions, risk and market context in one interface
description: An exploration of trading workflows, market information, risk management and trading tools within a unified interface.
summary: An independent exploration of what a trader needs in the first three seconds of looking at a screen: what is open, what is exposed, and what changed. TradingPal gathers market data, positions and risk into a single hierarchy instead of a wall of widgets, and studies how much information can be removed before a decision becomes harder to make.
challenge: Trading interfaces tend to optimise for data volume, which obscures the few signals that change a decision.
approach: A strict visual hierarchy for positions, exposure and market context, with charts and metrics sharing one reading order.
result: A design study in reducing a dashboard to the information a decision actually needs.

title: Rise
tagline: A life simulation where the economy pushes back
description: An interactive life-simulation game concept exploring virtual economies, world-building and player-driven experiences.
summary: Rise is a game concept about consequence. Instead of a world that waits for the player, the world keeps running: prices move, work dries up, relationships decay. The design question is how much simulation a player can feel without reading numbers, so most of the state is expressed through the environment and the people in it rather than through a panel.
challenge: Life simulations often surface their systems as spreadsheets, which turns play into administration.
approach: Simulated economies and relationships expressed through place, routine and dialogue instead of stat panels.
result: A world-building concept and interface direction for a player-driven economy.

title: ROOT//NODE
tagline: A messenger with no network at all
description: A one-shot optical messenger: one device flashes a message as a burst of QR symbols, the other reads it with its camera. No server, no account, no network.
summary: Every private messenger still needs an account, a relay server and a network path that can be observed, logged or blocked. ROOT//NODE removes all three. Each message is split into 80-byte chunks sealed with AES-GCM under an HKDF-SHA-256 handshake, with the frame index bound as additional authenticated data and a SHA-256 trailer closing the stream, so a dropped, reordered or spliced frame is rejected instead of silently accepted. Every symbol is rendered before playback begins, so nothing is encoded mid-flash.
challenge: Private messaging still depends on accounts, relay servers and a network path that can be watched or blocked.
approach: Chunked, authenticated payloads carried as a pre-rendered sequence of QR symbols between two screens and two cameras.
result: A working air-gapped channel shipped alongside an honest statement of what a browser application cannot protect.
